case_studies.title: Case-Specific Rubrics for Clinical AI Evaluation: Methodology, Validation, and LLM-Clinician Agreement Across 823 Encounters
case_studies.abstract: Objective. Clinical AI documentation systems require evaluation methodologies that are clinically valid, economically viable, and sensitive to iterative changes. Methods requiring expert review per scoring instance are too slow and expensive for safe, iterative deployment. We present a case-specific, clinician-authored rubric methodology for clinical AI evaluation and examine whether LLM-generated rubrics can approximate clinician agreement. Materials and Methods. Twenty clinicians authored 1,646 rubrics for 823 clinical cases (736 real-world, 87 synthetic) across primary care, psychiatry, onc
case_studies.summary: The problem of evaluating clinical AI documentation systems is addressed through a case-specific rubric methodology, which aims to provide a clinically valid, economically viable, and sensitive approach to iterative changes. The AI approach uses clinician-authored rubrics to evaluate clinical AI performance and examines the potential of LLM-generated rubrics to approximate clinician agreement. The outcome of this study shows promise in developing a more efficient and effective evaluation methodology for clinical AI systems.
case_studies.how_to_apply: AI practitioners can apply this methodology by collaborating with clinicians to develop case-specific rubrics for evaluating clinical AI performance, and exploring the use of LLM-generated rubrics to streamline the evaluation process. By doing so, they can improve the accuracy and efficiency of clinical AI evaluation, enabling safer and more iterative deployment of these systems.
case_studies.monetisation: The development of a case-specific rubric methodology for clinical AI evaluation presents a concrete business opportunity for companies specializing in healthcare AI solutions, as it can be integrated into their existing products to enhance evaluation and validation capabilities. Additionally, the potential for LLM-generated rubrics to approximate clinician agreement can be leveraged to create more efficient and cost-effective evaluation tools, generating revenue through subscription-based models or licensing agreements.

case_studies.title: Less Is More: Engineering Challenges of On-Device Small Language Model Integration in a Mobile Application
case_studies.abstract: On-device Small Language Models (SLMs) promise fully offline, private AI experiences for mobile users (no cloud dependency, no data leaving the device). But is this promise achievable in practice? This paper presents a longitudinal practitioner case study documenting the engineering challenges of integrating SLMs (Gemma 4 E2B, 2.6B parameters; Qwen3 0.6B, 600M parameters) into Palabrita, a production Android word-guessing game. Over a 5-day development sprint comprising 204 commits (~90 directly AI-related), the system underwent a radical transformation: from an ambitious design where the LLM
case_studies.summary: The case study explores the engineering challenges of integrating Small Language Models (SLMs) into a mobile application, specifically a word-guessing game called Palabrita. The authors used a longitudinal practitioner case study approach, documenting the integration of two SLMs, Gemma 4 E2B and Qwen3, into the game. The outcome of the study highlights the potential and limitations of using SLMs in mobile applications, providing valuable insights for practitioners.
case_studies.how_to_apply: To apply the lessons from this study, AI practitioners should carefully evaluate the trade-offs between model size, accuracy, and computational resources when integrating SLMs into mobile applications. By doing so, they can design and develop more efficient and effective AI-powered mobile applications that provide seamless user experiences.
case_studies.monetisation: The study's findings have significant monetisation potential, as they can inform the development of AI-powered mobile applications that provide unique and private user experiences, potentially attracting premium users willing to pay for such features. By leveraging the insights from this study, companies can create new revenue streams and differentiate their products in a crowded market.

case_studies.title: Characterizing Vision-Language-Action Models across XPUs: Constraints and Acceleration for On-Robot Deployment
case_studies.abstract: Vision-Language-Action (VLA) models are promising for generalist robot control, but on-robot deployment is bottlenecked by real-time inference under tight cost and energy budgets. Most prior evaluations rely on desktop-grade GPUs, obscuring the trade-offs and opportunities offered by heterogeneous edge accelerators (GPUs/XPUs/NPUs). We present a systematic analysis for low-cost VLA deployment via model-hardware co-characterization. First, we build a cross-accelerator leaderboard and evaluate model-hardware pairs under CET (Cost, Energy, Time), showing that right-sized edge devices can be more
case_studies.summary: The problem of real-time inference in Vision-Language-Action models for on-robot deployment is addressed through a systematic analysis of model-hardware co-characterization. The AI approach involves building a cross-accelerator leaderboard to evaluate model-hardware pairs under constraints of cost, energy, and time. The outcome shows that right-sized edge devices can be more efficient for low-cost VLA deployment.
case_studies.how_to_apply: AI practitioners can apply this lesson by considering the co-characterization of models and hardware to optimize for cost, energy, and time in their own deployments. This involves evaluating model-hardware pairs on various edge accelerators to find the most efficient combination for their specific use case.
case_studies.monetisation: A concrete business opportunity lies in developing and marketing optimized Vision-Language-Action models for on-robot deployment, targeting industries that require efficient and cost-effective robot control. Companies can also offer customized model-hardware co-characterization services to help clients find the most suitable edge devices for their specific applications.

case_studies.title: AgentPulse: A Continuous Multi-Signal Framework for Evaluating AI Agents in Deployment
case_studies.abstract: Static benchmarks measure what AI agents can do at a fixed point in time but not how they are adopted, maintained, or experienced in deployment. We introduce AgentPulse, a continuous evaluation framework scoring 50 agents across 10 workload categories along four factors (Benchmark Performance, Adoption Signals, Community Sentiment, and Ecosystem Health) aggregated from 18 real-time signals across GitHub, package registries, IDE marketplaces, social platforms, and benchmark leaderboards. Three analyses ground the framework. The four factors capture largely complementary information (n=50; $ρ_{\
case_studies.summary: The problem of evaluating AI agents in deployment is addressed through a continuous multi-signal framework, AgentPulse, which assesses agents across various factors. The AI approach involves aggregating real-time signals from multiple sources, including GitHub and social platforms, to provide a comprehensive evaluation. The outcome is a framework that captures complementary information, enabling a more nuanced understanding of AI agents in deployment.
case_studies.how_to_apply: AI practitioners can apply the lessons from AgentPulse by incorporating multiple signals and factors into their evaluation frameworks, allowing for a more comprehensive assessment of AI agents. By doing so, they can gain a better understanding of their agents' performance, adoption, and overall health in deployment.
case_studies.monetisation: The AgentPulse framework presents a concrete business opportunity for companies to develop and offer evaluation and monitoring services for AI agents, helping organizations optimize their AI deployments. This could be achieved through the creation of a product or platform that leverages the AgentPulse framework, providing valuable insights and recommendations for AI agent improvement.

case_studies.title: On-Device Vision Training, Deployment, and Inference on a Thumb-Sized Microcontroller
case_studies.abstract: This paper presents a complete, end-to-end on-device vision machine learning pipeline, comprising data acquisition, two-layer CNN training with Adam optimization, and real-time inference, executing entirely on a microcontroller-class device costing $15-40 USD. Unlike cloud-based workflows that require external infrastructure and conceal the computational pipeline from the practitioner, this system implements every step of the core ML lifecycle in approximately 1,750 lines of readable C++ that compiles in under one minute using the Arduino IDE, with no external ML dependencies. Running on the S
case_studies.summary: The problem addressed in this paper is the need for a complete, end-to-end on-device vision machine learning pipeline that can run on low-cost, microcontroller-class devices. The AI approach used is a two-layer CNN trained with Adam optimization, which is implemented entirely on the device. The outcome is a system that can perform real-time inference, executing every step of the core ML lifecycle in a compact and efficient manner.
case_studies.how_to_apply: AI practitioners can apply the lessons from this paper by focusing on developing end-to-end pipelines that can run on resource-constrained devices, allowing for greater flexibility and autonomy in AI-powered systems. This can be achieved by leveraging optimized algorithms and compact code implementations, such as the 1,750 lines of readable C++ used in this study.
case_studies.monetisation: The development of this on-device vision machine learning pipeline presents a concrete business opportunity for creating low-cost, intelligent devices that can be used in a variety of applications, such as industrial automation or consumer electronics. Companies can leverage this technology to create innovative products that combine computer vision and machine learning capabilities with the benefits of low power consumption and small form factor.

case_studies.title: A Deployable Embodied Vision-Language Navigation System with Hierarchical Cognition and Context-Aware Exploration
case_studies.abstract: Bridging the gap between embodied intelligence and embedded deployment remains a key challenge in intelligent robotic systems, where perception, reasoning, and planning must operate under strict constraints on computation, memory, energy, and real-time execution. In vision-language navigation (VLN), existing approaches often face a fundamental trade-off between strong reasoning capabilities and efficient deployment on real-world platforms. In this paper, we present a deployable embodied VLN system that achieves both high efficiency and robust high-level reasoning on real-world robotic platform
case_studies.summary: The problem of bridging the gap between embodied intelligence and embedded deployment in intelligent robotic systems is addressed in this paper. The authors propose a deployable embodied vision-language navigation system that achieves both high efficiency and robust high-level reasoning on real-world robotic platforms using hierarchical cognition and context-aware exploration. The outcome is a system that can operate under strict constraints on computation, memory, energy, and real-time execution.
case_studies.how_to_apply: To apply this research, AI practitioners can focus on developing hierarchical cognition and context-aware exploration mechanisms for their robotic systems, allowing for more efficient and robust navigation. By integrating vision-language navigation with embodied intelligence, practitioners can create more effective and deployable robotic systems for real-world applications.
case_studies.monetisation: The proposed system has potential for monetisation in industries such as robotics, autonomous vehicles, and smart homes, where efficient and robust navigation is crucial. Companies can adapt this technology to create products such as autonomous cleaning robots or smart home assistants that can navigate and interact with their environment effectively.

case_studies.title: FastOMOP: A Foundational Architecture for Reliable Agentic Real-World Evidence Generation on OMOP CDM data
case_studies.abstract: The Observational Medical Outcomes Partnership Common Data Model (OMOP CDM), maintained by the Observational Health Data Sciences and Informatics (OHDSI) collaboration, enabled the harmonisation of electronic health records data of nearly one billion patients in 83 countries. Yet generating real-world evidence (RWE) from these repositories remains a manual process requiring clinical, epidemiological and technical expertise. LLMs and multi-agent systems have shown promise for clinical tasks, but RWE automation exposes a fundamental challenge: agentic systems introduce emergent behaviours, coord
case_studies.summary: The generation of real-world evidence from electronic health records data is a manual process that requires significant clinical, epidemiological, and technical expertise. The authors propose using Large Language Models (LLMs) and multi-agent systems to automate this process, addressing the challenge of agentic systems introducing emergent behaviors. The proposed architecture, FastOMOP, aims to provide a foundational framework for reliable and efficient real-world evidence generation on OMOP CDM data.
case_studies.how_to_apply: To apply this approach, AI practitioners should focus on designing and developing architectures that can accommodate the complexities of agentic systems and their emergent behaviors. By leveraging LLMs and multi-agent systems, practitioners can create more efficient and reliable systems for generating real-world evidence from large-scale health data repositories.
case_studies.monetisation: The proposed FastOMOP architecture presents a significant business opportunity for companies operating in the healthcare and pharmaceutical industries, as it can help reduce the costs and time associated with manual real-world evidence generation. By developing and commercializing this technology, companies can offer valuable services to healthcare organizations, pharmaceutical companies, and research institutions, enabling them to make more informed decisions and drive better patient outcomes.
case_studies.relevance_tag: AI Agents, LLMs, Automation, Healthcare AI

case_studies.title: GradMAP: Gradient-Based Multi-Agent Proximal Learning for Grid-Edge Flexibility
case_studies.abstract: Coordinating large populations of grid-edge devices requires learning methods that remain fully decentralised in deployment while still respecting three-phase AC distribution-network physics. This paper proposes gradient-based multi-agent proximal learning (GradMAP) to address this challenge. GradMAP trains independent neural-network policies for each agent without any parameter sharing, and each agent uses only its own local observation for online decision-making without communication. During offline training, GradMAP embeds a differentiable three-phase AC power-flow model in a primal-dual le
case_studies.summary: The problem of coordinating large populations of grid-edge devices is addressed through a novel AI approach called GradMAP, which trains independent neural-network policies for each agent without any parameter sharing. GradMAP uses a differentiable three-phase AC power-flow model in a primal-dual learning framework to enable decentralised decision-making. The outcome is a fully decentralised learning method that respects three-phase AC distribution-network physics, allowing for more efficient and flexible grid management.
case_studies.how_to_apply: AI practitioners can apply the GradMAP approach by embedding differentiable physical models into their learning frameworks, enabling decentralised decision-making in complex systems. This can be particularly useful in applications where real-time communication between agents is not feasible, such as in grid-edge device coordination or other distributed control systems.
case_studies.monetisation: The GradMAP approach has potential for monetisation in the smart grid and energy management sectors, where decentralised control and optimisation of grid-edge devices can lead to significant efficiency gains and cost savings. Companies developing grid management systems or energy optimisation platforms could integrate GradMAP into their products to improve their competitive advantage and offer more effective solutions to their customers.

case_studies.title: Large-scale wireless network management via Open-RAN Tandem Apps: Cell on/off switching use case
case_studies.abstract: With growing mobile-network complexity, management and optimization have become increasingly difficult. Centralized algorithms face high control-data overhead and computational load, while distributed approaches often perform far from optimally. The O-RAN architecture introduces two tiers of RAN Intelligent Controllers (RICs), enabling hierarchical network-management schemes. This work proposes Tandem Apps: a pair of tightly coupled optimization mechanisms running on both controllers. We show how to design Tandem Apps through architectural and functional splitting to achieve an agile, low-comp
case_studies.summary: The management and optimization of large-scale wireless networks have become increasingly difficult due to growing mobile-network complexity. This work proposes the use of Tandem Apps, a pair of tightly coupled optimization mechanisms running on both RAN Intelligent Controllers (RICs) in the O-RAN architecture, to achieve agile and low-complexity network management. The proposed approach shows promise in addressing the challenges of centralized and distributed network management approaches.
case_studies.how_to_apply: To apply this approach, AI practitioners can utilize the O-RAN architecture and design Tandem Apps through architectural and functional splitting to achieve hierarchical network-management schemes. By leveraging the proposed approach, practitioners can develop more efficient and scalable network management solutions.
case_studies.monetisation: The proposed Tandem Apps approach has the potential to be monetized as a product or service, offering wireless network operators a more efficient and scalable solution for network management. This could be achieved through partnerships with network operators or by developing a standalone product that can be integrated into existing network management systems.

case_studies.title: Diffusion Templates: A Unified Plugin Framework for Controllable Diffusion
case_studies.abstract: Controllable diffusion methods have substantially expanded the practical utility of diffusion models, but they are typically developed as isolated, backbone-specific systems with incompatible training pipelines, parameter formats, and runtime hooks. This fragmentation makes it difficult to reuse infrastructure across tasks, transfer capabilities across backbones, or compose multiple controls within a single generation pipeline. We present Diffusion Templates, a unified and open plugin framework that decouples base-model inference from controllable capability injection. The framework is organiz
case_studies.summary: The problem of controllable diffusion methods being developed as isolated systems with incompatible training pipelines and parameter formats is addressed through the introduction of Diffusion Templates. This unified plugin framework decouples base-model inference from controllable capability injection, enabling the reuse of infrastructure and transfer of capabilities across different backbones. The outcome is a more flexible and efficient approach to controllable diffusion methods, allowing for the composition of multiple controls within a single generation pipeline.
case_studies.how_to_apply: AI practitioners can apply the Diffusion Templates framework by integrating it into their existing diffusion model pipelines, enabling the injection of controllable capabilities and transfer of capabilities across different backbones. By decoupling base-model inference from controllable capability injection, practitioners can develop more flexible and efficient controllable diffusion methods.
case_studies.monetisation: The Diffusion Templates framework presents a concrete business opportunity for companies developing AI-powered generation tools, such as image and video generation platforms, by providing a unified and efficient approach to controllable diffusion methods. This can be monetised through the development of commercial plugins and APIs that leverage the Diffusion Templates framework, offering customers more flexibility and control over their AI-powered generation workflows.

case_studies.title: Joint Sato-Tate Laws for Transformations of Hecke Eigenvalues: The Vertical Case
case_studies.abstract: We introduce a framework within which a large class of joint equidistribution problems can be studied and resolved with effective error terms. This involves proving a higher dimensional and $μ$-analogue of the Erdös-Turán inequality, and utilizing the theory of the Hardy-Krause (H-K) variation from analysis, where, in particular, we formulate a technique to approximate a broad class of relevant functions by functions of bounded H-K variation. Our main focus will be on the vertical Sato-Tate problem for spaces of cusp forms and for families of elliptic curves over finite fields. In particular,
case_studies.summary: The problem addressed in this study is the joint equidistribution of Hecke eigenvalues, which is a fundamental question in number theory. The AI approach involves utilizing the theory of the Hardy-Krause variation and formulating a technique to approximate relevant functions. The outcome is a framework for studying and resolving a large class of joint equidistribution problems with effective error terms.
case_studies.how_to_apply: Practitioners can apply the techniques developed in this study by utilizing the Hardy-Krause variation theory to approximate complex functions and solve equidistribution problems in their own domains. This requires a deep understanding of mathematical analysis and number theory, as well as the ability to adapt these techniques to new problems.
case_studies.monetisation: A potential business opportunity based on this research could involve developing software or consulting services that help organizations solve complex equidistribution problems in fields such as cryptography or coding theory. However, the abstract nature of the research and the lack of clear metrics or product opportunities make it challenging to monetize this study directly.

case_studies.title: Learning to Think from Multiple Thinkers
case_studies.abstract: We study learning with Chain-of-Thought (CoT) supervision from multiple thinkers, all of whom provide correct but possibly systematically different solutions, e.g., step-by-step solutions to math problems written by different thinkers, or step-by-step execution traces of different programs solving the same problem. We consider classes that are computationally easy to learn using CoT supervision from a single thinker, but hard to learn with only end-result supervision, i.e., without CoT (Joshi et al. 2025). We establish that, under cryptographic assumptions, learning can be hard from CoT superv
case_studies.summary: The problem addressed in this study is the difficulty of learning from Chain-of-Thought supervision when multiple thinkers provide different solutions. The AI approach involves analyzing the learning process from multiple thinkers and establishing the hardness of learning under cryptographic assumptions. The outcome of this study provides insights into the limitations of learning with Chain-of-Thought supervision from multiple thinkers.
case_studies.how_to_apply: AI practitioners can apply the lessons from this study by considering the potential biases and differences in thinking styles when using Chain-of-Thought supervision from multiple thinkers. To overcome these challenges, practitioners can explore techniques such as data augmentation, ensemble methods, or adversarial training to improve the robustness of their models.
case_studies.monetisation: A potential business opportunity arising from this research is the development of more robust and adaptive AI models that can learn from diverse thinkers, which can be applied in areas such as education, healthcare, or finance. Companies can leverage these advancements to create personalized learning platforms, decision-support systems, or expert-augmentation tools that can learn from and adapt to multiple thinking styles.

case_studies.title: Can Current Agents Close the Discovery-to-Application Gap? A Case Study in Minecraft
case_studies.abstract: Discovering causal regularities and applying them to build functional systems--the discovery-to-application loop--is a hallmark of general intelligence, yet evaluating this capacity has been hindered by the vast complexity gap between scientific discovery and real-world engineering. We introduce SciCrafter, a Minecraft-based benchmark that operationalizes this loop through parameterized redstone circuit tasks. Agents must ignite lamps in specified patterns (e.g., simultaneously or in timed sequences); scaling target parameters substantially increases construction complexity and required knowle
case_studies.summary: The discovery-to-application gap is a significant challenge in achieving general intelligence, where agents must discover causal regularities and apply them to build functional systems. To address this, the authors introduce SciCrafter, a Minecraft-based benchmark that operationalizes this loop through parameterized redstone circuit tasks. The outcome of this study provides insights into the capabilities of current agents in closing the discovery-to-application gap.
case_studies.how_to_apply: AI practitioners can apply the lessons from this study by using Minecraft-based benchmarks to evaluate the capabilities of their agents in discovering causal regularities and applying them to build functional systems. By using parameterized tasks, practitioners can scale the complexity of the tasks and assess the performance of their agents in a more comprehensive manner.
case_studies.monetisation: The SciCrafter benchmark has the potential to be monetized as a tool for evaluating the performance of AI agents, particularly in the context of robotics and automation. Companies can use SciCrafter to test the capabilities of their AI systems and identify areas for improvement, providing a concrete business opportunity for the development of more advanced AI agents.

case_studies.title: Measuring Successful Cooperation in Human-AI Teamwork: Development and Validation of the Perceived Cooperativity and Teaming Perception Scales
case_studies.abstract: As human-AI cooperation becomes increasingly prevalent, reliable instruments for assessing the subjective quality of cooperative human-AI interaction are needed. We introduce two theoretically grounded scales: the Perceived Cooperativity Scale (PCS), grounded in joint activity theory, and the Teaming Perception Scale (TPS), grounded in evolutionary cooperation theory. The PCS captures an agent's perceived cooperative capability and practice within a single interaction sequence; the TPS captures the emergent sense of teaming arising from mutual contribution and support. Both scales were adapted
case_studies.summary: The problem of evaluating human-AI cooperation has become increasingly important as AI becomes more prevalent in various industries. The authors propose two scales, the Perceived Cooperativity Scale (PCS) and the Teaming Perception Scale (TPS), to assess the subjective quality of cooperative human-AI interaction. The outcome of this research provides a foundation for developing reliable instruments to measure the success of human-AI teamwork.
case_studies.how_to_apply: AI practitioners can apply the concepts of joint activity theory and evolutionary cooperation theory to develop more effective human-AI collaboration systems. By using the PCS and TPS scales, practitioners can evaluate and improve the cooperative capabilities of their AI systems, leading to more successful human-AI teamwork.
case_studies.monetisation: The development of reliable instruments for assessing human-AI cooperation can lead to new business opportunities in fields such as AI-powered customer service, collaborative robotics, and autonomous vehicles. Companies can utilize the PCS and TPS scales to evaluate and improve their AI systems, increasing their competitiveness and potential for revenue growth.

case_studies.title: Multiple positive solutions with prescribed masses for a coupled Schrödinger system: mass mixed and Sobolev critical coupled case
case_studies.abstract: The aim of this paper is to establish multiple positive normalized solutions $(u,v,λ_1,λ_2)\in H^1(\mathbb{R}^N,\mathbb{R}^2)\times \mathbb{R}^2$ to the following coupled Schrödinger system involving Sobolev critical exponent: $$ \begin{cases} -Δu+λ_1 u=μ_1|u|^{p-2}u+να|u|^{α-2}u|v|^β, x\in \mathbb{R}^N,\\ -Δv+λ_2 v=μ_2|v|^{q-2}v+νβ|v|^{β-2}v|u|^α, x\in \mathbb{R}^N,\\ \int_{\mathbb{R}^N}|u|^2\mathrm{d}x=a, \int_{\mathbb{R}^N}|v|^2\mathrm{d}x=b, \end{cases} N\geq 3, $$ where $μ_1,μ_2, ν, a, b>0$. case_studies.summary: This paper investigates a coupled Schrödinger system with prescribed masses, focusing on the mass mixed and Sobolev critical coupled case. The authors employ mathematical analysis and variational methods to establish multiple positive normalized solutions. The outcome contributes to the understanding of the system's behavior and properties, particularly in the context of coupled Schrödinger equations.
case_studies.how_to_apply: AI practitioners can apply the mathematical framework and variational methods used in this paper to analyze and solve similar problems in other fields, such as physics or engineering. By understanding the behavior of coupled systems, researchers can develop more accurate models and predictions.
case_studies.monetisation: While this research is primarily academic, it can potentially lead to breakthroughs in fields like quantum computing or materials science, which can have significant commercial applications. Companies involved in these areas can explore partnerships with researchers or invest in further development of these ideas.
